Title: Diagnosis of test `testGenerateURLFragment`
Details: The test `testGenerateURLFragment` checks whether HTML entities such as `"` are correctly escaped to their corresponding character by the `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` method. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case. Following the execution path, we find that `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` is not escaping any HTML code; instead, it is using its input `toolTipText` as is. Consequently, un-escaped strings are being returned, which leads to the error demonstrated by the test.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis of test `testHWRuleEx1`

Details: The test `testHWRuleEx1` verifies that the Soundex encoding version implementing the "HW rule" correctly encodes names according to historical census rules. In particular, it checks that "Ashcraft" and "Ashcroft" both encode to "A261" and that the "H" and "W" characters between consonants are treated properly to avoid incorrect encodings. The test fails, indicating a mismatch in the Soundex encoding output.

The `Soundex.encode(String)` method calls `Soundex.soundex(String)` which performs the core encoding. This method cleans the input string and uses a character array `out` to build the Soundex code, starting with the first letter, then encoding the rest using `getMappingCode`.

The important logic involves `getMappingCode(String, int)` which maps the character at the given index in the string to a Soundex digit using `map(char)`. It also applies the "HW rule": if the current character is not the first or second character and is not mapped to '0', and if the previous character is 'H' or 'W', it looks at the character before the previous one. If this "pre-HW" character maps to the same code as the current character or is itself 'H' or 'W', it returns 0 to skip this character in the encoding.

The mapping array `US_ENGLISH_MAPPING` uses the string "01230120022455012623010202" as its basis, mapping letters A-Z to codes.

The diagnosis is that the failure in test `testHWRuleEx1` stems from the implementation of the "HW rule" inside the `getMappingCode` method. The condition in lines 191-193 is:

```
if (firstCode == mappedChar || 'H' == preHWChar || 'W' == preHWChar) {
  return 0;
}
```

which returns 0 (skip code) if the mapping code of the character two places back or "preHWChar" is 'H' or 'W', or if the mapping code matches `mappedChar`. This simple rule is too broad or incorrect for all cases, causing the test failure.

Therefore, the underlying bug lies within the logic of `Soundex.getMappingCode(String, int)` that applies the "HW rule". The mapping function and the rest of the Soundex encoding are functioning as intended according to standard mappings, but the "HW rule" is misapplied as per the historical census rules example in the test.

The place to fix the bug is the method `org.apache.commons.codec.language.Soundex.getMappingCode(java.lang.String,int)` which incorrectly filters characters according to the "HW rule".

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
